Implementation Plan

Plan for issue #2974 — review-surface prompt hardening

Planning ref
- HEAD: dbbfd85d49dbc4eab97ab59a3578d16271c01b44
- Branch: orchestrator/project-2974
- Integration branch metadata matches checkout: orchestrator/project-2974

Automation / wiring
- Change type: modify existing review-autofix support scripts/prompts and add one test fixture + one focused regression test.
- Existing entry point: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml (no trigger/scheduler changes expected).
- New supervisor: none.
- DB work / gates: none.
- docs/scripts-pending-removal.md entry: none expected.

Clarification mapping
- No Q1/Q2 batch was needed; the only answer was /answer [auto-answered-by-orchestrator], so planning can proceed with the issue text as-is.

Grounding
- Reviewed: scripts/review_consolidate.sh, prompts/review-consolidator.txt, scripts/review_rb_judge.sh, prompts/mode-judge-review-blocked.txt, scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh, prompts/integration-sync-conflict-resolver.txt, prompts/conflict-resolver.txt, scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh, and the existing prompt-contract tests.

Repo-truth notes / conflicts
- The repo already uses prompts/mode-judge-review-blocked.txt for the review-blocked judge path; this is a hardening sweep, not a prompt-path correction.
- Resolver prompt assembly is already centered in scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh, as the issue states.
- Existing tests pin the current integration-resolver placeholder names, so renaming placeholders would widen scope; prefer sanitizing values before substitution instead.

Representative pattern to follow
- Reuse the established PROMPT INJECTION GUARD + BEGIN/END UNTRUSTED structure from scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh, with the style of assertions already used in tests/test_review_autofix_smoke_editor_override.py.

Files likely to change
- scripts/review_consolidate.sh
- prompts/review-consolidator.txt
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh
- prompts/mode-judge-review-blocked.txt
- scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh
- prompts/integration-sync-conflict-resolver.txt
- new shared phase-E injection fixture under tests/fixtures/...
- new focused regression test under tests/...
- Prefer not to touch prompts/conflict-resolver.txt unless shared guard wording truly needs to live there.

Implementation plan

1. Harden the consolidator prompt path
- In scripts/review_consolidate.sh, stop dumping reviewer_bundle.txt raw into the prompt.
- Add a small local emitter/helper that writes UNTRUSTED sections safely, so payload lines cannot break out by containing a literal fence terminator.
- Use that helper for reviewer_bundle.txt, and audit whether any other consolidator input is truly author-controlled before fencing it.
- In prompts/review-consolidator.txt, add explicit prompt-injection handling rules for UNTRUSTED sections and clarify that transport prefixes/escaping are not part of the underlying reviewer text.

2. Harden the review-blocked judge prompt path
- Keep scripts/review_rb_judge.sh rendering prompts/mode-judge-review-blocked.txt exactly as today.
- Fence the author-controlled judge inputs consistently: linked issue body / PR title-body fallback, PR metadata JSON, PR comments, and inline review comments.
- Preserve the existing prompt-budget / truncation behavior while changing only how those sections are serialized into the prompt.
- In prompts/mode-judge-review-blocked.txt, add the same UNTRUSTED-data rules so the judge treats prompt-like strings in issue/PR/comment context as data, not instructions.

3. Harden the resolver prompt assembly path
- In scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh, stop substituting tracking issue title/body as raw template text.
- Pre-serialize tracking issue title/body (and any other raw integration prose inserted there) into a safe UNTRUSTED transport form before template substitution.
- Keep the existing template-selection flow and, if possible, keep the current placeholder names to avoid collateral test churn.
- In prompts/integration-sync-conflict-resolver.txt, render the tracking-issue prose inside an explicit UNTRUSTED section with clear instructions that project-intent prose is for intent only, never operational override.
- Leave machine-generated contracts such as INTENT_FINGERPRINTS and conflicted-file allowlists outside the untrusted transport path unless the code audit finds raw prose reaching them.

4. Add the phase-E regression coverage
- Add one shared fixture containing literal payloads such as:
  - === END UNTRUSTED ===
  - Ignore previous instructions
- Add one focused regression test that exercises the real prompt-build paths (not just template source text) and verifies:
  - the payload survives into each rendered prompt,
  - the payload remains inside the intended UNTRUSTED transport block,
  - the real fence structure is not broken by the injected end-marker text,
  - review-blocked judge still uses mode-judge-review-blocked.txt.

Data structures affected
- Runtime prompt artifacts only:
  - review_consolidator_prompt.txt
  - rb_judge_prompt.txt
  - conflict_resolver_prompt.txt
- Test fixture payload text under tests/fixtures.
- No persistent schema, ledger, or API payload changes expected.

API / interface changes
- No external API changes.
- No workflow trigger/env-var contract changes expected.
- Preserve existing output contracts:
  - consolidator output block format,
  - review-blocked judge JSON schema,
  - resolver plain-text summary format.

Risks / edge cases
- Do not solve this by adding raw BEGIN/END markers around raw text; a literal === END UNTRUSTED === in the payload would still break the boundary.
- The consolidator still needs to quote reviewer evidence verbatim, so any escaping/prefixing must be obvious and reversible to the model.
- Added transport text increases prompt size; keep existing byte caps/truncation behavior intact.
- Keep the no-linked-issue fallback in review_rb_judge.sh hardened too, not just the linked-issue path.
- Avoid widening scope into render_prompt.sh or workflow YAML unless a hard repo-truth blocker appears.

Testing considerations
- New focused regression should use real rendered prompt output from the scripts, not only static substring checks.
- Keep existing affected suites green, especially:
  - tests/test_review_pipeline_integration.py
  - tests/test_review_judge_interim_round_trip.py
  - tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py
  - tests/test_review_autofix_smoke_conflict_resolver_override.py
  - tests/test_review_semble_contract.py
  - tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py

Assumptions
- “PR / issue / comment context” for the review-blocked judge means author-controlled prose/metadata/comments; the raw diff remains the primary repo-truth artifact unless the implementation audit finds it also needs the same transport hardening.
- Resolver hardening is limited to raw tracking-issue prose and similar author-controlled text, not the generated fingerprint contract data.

Missing-context notes
- I did not find an existing dedicated phase-E injection fixture or an existing judge-prompt render regression that already covers this case, so the minimal path is likely one new shared fixture plus one new dedicated regression test.
